headline: DRC HALTS ALL COBALT EXPORTS STARTING NOV 30 — Four-Month Ban Covers 75% of World Supply as Prices Surge
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo will reimpose a full ban on cobalt exports from November 30, 2026, citing a 'significant and sustained decline' in prices driven by oversupply, slowing EV demand, and speculative market practices. Industry regulator ARECOMS confirmed the ban will last four months and covers industrial, semi-industrial and artisanal output — a move that removes approximately 75% of global mined cobalt supply from the market. Cobalt prices have already begun spiking in physical markets as buyers scramble to secure pre-ban inventory.

headline: CMOC RUSHES COBALT SHIPMENTS BEFORE DRC BAN KICKS IN — World's Largest Cobalt Miner Races November 30 Deadline
snippet: CMOC, operator of the Tenke Fungurume mine and the world's largest cobalt producer by volume, has moved to accelerate cobalt shipments out of the DRC before the country's November 30 export ban takes effect. The rush to export ahead of the deadline underscores the severity of the coming supply disruption: CMOC's DRC operations produce a significant share of global cobalt, and any halt in its shipments directly tightens the market for a metal critical to lithium-ion EV batteries.

headline: GOLD MINERS HISTORICALLY CHEAP AS EARNINGS DEFY RISING COSTS — GDXJ at 77.5% of 200-Day MA, Most Oversold in 4 Years
snippet: An Investing.com analysis published November 27 argues that gold mining stocks are trading at historical valuation discounts despite Q3 earnings that largely defied rising input costs. The GDXJ closed at just 77.5% of its 200-day moving average — the most oversold junior gold miners have been in four years — even as underlying earnings remain solid at $3,500+ gold. The analysis identifies the disconnect between strong fundamentals and deeply depressed valuations as a potential generational contrarian entry point.

headline: FLYNN GOLD HITS 28M @ 1.61g/t IN FIRST BRILLIANT PROSPECT HOLE — ASX Junior Eyes 2027 Resource at Tasmania Discovery
snippet: Flynn Gold (ASX: FG1) reported its first significant drill result at the Brilliant Prospect in Tasmania on November 25, with hole BRDD018 returning 28 metres at 1.61 g/t gold from 74 metres depth. The company targets a first gold resource estimate in 2027. The result adds to growing investor interest in Tasmanian gold, a jurisdiction that has historically underexplored relative to its geological prospectivity.

headline: CHALLENGER GOLD CONFIRMS MINE MODEL WITH 57.7M @ 1.31g/t AT HUALILÁN — Argentine Flagship Hits 7.1M @ 5.22g/t High-Grade Interval
snippet: Challenger Gold (ASX: CEL) released initial results from its 35,000-metre program at the Hualilán project in San Juan Province, Argentina, with the first ten holes confirming the company's existing mine study model. Hole GNDD873 returned 57.7 metres at 1.31 grams per tonne gold equivalent, including a high-grade interval of 7.1 metres at 5.22 g/t AuEq. The consistent grade and geometry across early holes support the feasibility of an open-pittable oxide deposit.

headline: DRC ENFORCES 2018 LOCAL OWNERSHIP LAW — 10% Congolese Citizen Stake Now Mandatory on Top of State Mining Shares
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo has announced it will begin enforcing a 2018 law requiring Congolese citizens to hold at least 10% of mining company shares on top of mandatory state ownership. The regulation has been dormant since passage due to implementation challenges, but its activation adds a new compliance layer for miners already navigating the country's imminent cobalt export ban and persistent political instability. Junior and mid-tier miners with significant DRC operations face the most direct impact on deal structures and capital raises.

headline: INFINITY METALS ACQUIRES UNDRILLED COPPER TARGET IN W.A. — ASX:INF Binding Deal for Nanadie North Adds to M&A Wave
snippet: Infinity Metals (ASX: INF) has entered a binding agreement to acquire the Nanadie North copper target in Western Australia — an undrilled prospect with historical surface anomalies in a region known for significant copper systems. The deal closes as ASX junior copper developers trade at significant discounts to intrinsic value, drawing opportunistic acquirers to undrilled ground. The acquisition remains subject to customary regulatory conditions.

headline: SCORPION MINERALS BUYS 289 SQ KM PAYNES FIND GOLD — W.A. Junior Extends Land Grab in Murchison Goldfield
snippet: Scorpion Minerals (ASX: SCN) has signed a binding deal to acquire 100% of the Paynes Find Gold Project, a 289-square-kilometre package in Western Australia's historically productive Murchison goldfield. The acquisition extends Scorpion's land position in a district attracting renewed exploration spending as gold prices hold above $3,500 per ounce. The company adds the project to an existing Western Australian portfolio at a time when junior gold developers remain deeply undervalued relative to both bullion and comparable producer valuations.
